dedupe_keys.name: antwerp heat stress adaptation based on detailed thermal mapping urbclim

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes how the City of Antwerp, Belgium, used detailed thermal mapping to plan heat stress adaptation. The research organisation VITO applied its UrbClim urban climate model at 100 m resolution, as it had for 100 European cities in the Copernicus European Health service, showing an urban heat island averaging 2 degrees C in the centre and reaching 9 degrees C on summer evenings and nights. Measures were set at three scales: city-wide changes to the building code, local green roofs, trees, unpaved surfaces, ponds and fountains, and a heat forecast and warning system and citizen science campaigns aimed at vulnerable people. Research ran from 2013, funded mainly by the EU projects RAMSES, NACLIM, Climate-fit.city and Ground Truth 2.0, with one city-funded measurement and modelling study costing about 70,000 euro. The page is free HTML on the Climate-ADAPT portal (2020). Caveats: many measures were only starting or planned, city-wide results are expected by 2030, and communication and technical integration remain challenges. It illustrates how urban climate model outputs feed green infrastructure and early warning planning for heat; a related record is the UMEP urban climate tool.
name: Antwerp heat stress adaptation based on detailed thermal mapping (UrbClim)
notes: The UMEP record is on another branch or the integrator and is named in prose only.
outcomes: Heat maps showed an urban heat island of 2 degrees C on average and up to 9 degrees C, leading to a revised building code, local greening measures and a heat warning system feeding the Climate 2030 plan.
provider: Climate-ADAPT (European Environment Agency), case study on the City of Antwerp and VITO
